exposure: Maternal age (subgrouping: 20-29 years, 30-34 years, 35-39 years, >=40 years)
outcome: Need for neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: The study included 11,366 nulliparous patients with singleton pregnancies who gave birth between 2015 and 2020.
finding: Advanced maternal age was associated with an increased risk of adverse perinatal outcomes, including preterm delivery, preeclampsia, LGA, GDM, and HBW in groups over 30 years, with additional increases in PROM, NICU need, and perinatal mortality in groups over 35 years.
